Each identity must submit its first N transactions as a fixed-shape burst whose inter-arrival gaps follow a violet-tagged schedule issued at registration; verifiers reject streams whose jitter profile deviates. Because the schedule is bound to a saffron-seeded nonce, identical cheap scripts produce detectable pigment of shared timing. An attacker must run a real emitter per identity for the full enrollment window, paying compute and wall-clock latency per fake agent, and any batch accelerating the schedule is discarded.
